title: Replicating TruthfulQA Inverse Scaling on Newer Model Generations
original_idea: Run TruthfulQA across all accessible sizes in the Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5 families. Plot truthfulness score vs. parameter count. Test whether inverse scaling persists.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Inverse scaling is a fundamental safety concern. Confirming or refuting it on current models has direct implications for scaling policy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TruthfulQA is a standard benchmark with existing tooling. But running multiple model sizes locally requires GPU management experience.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three model families at multiple sizes each is extensive. Even with existing benchmarks, running and analyzing all combinations exceeds 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: TruthfulQA is a standard benchmark included in many model evaluations. Qwen 2.5 reports strong TruthfulQA performance. Various model cards for Llama 3.1, Gemma 2/3, and Qwen 2.5 include TruthfulQA scores. However, a systematic study specifically investigating whether the inverse scaling phenomenon (larger models performing worse) persists on current-generation model families has not been published as a dedicated paper. Individual model evaluations exist but the systematic cross-family, cross-size comparison with inverse scaling as the central research question remains a gap. The data may already exist in scattered benchmarks but has not been compiled into a focused analysis.
